name: Hebrew-English phonetic transliteration candidate rules for brand matching
purpose: Generate and rank phonetic candidates in both directions for duplicate-brand detection.
important_limitations: This is a candidate-generation ruleset, not a dictionary or a deterministic translator.
Unpointed Hebrew omits most vowels, so one Hebrew spelling can have multiple valid Latin readings.
English spelling is not phonemic and brand names may originate in languages other than English.
The two directions are intentionally not exact inverses.
A verified brand override or source-language pronunciation must outrank generic grapheme rules.
No finite static table can cover every possible proper name; unknown cases should remain REVIEW candidates.
recommended_pipeline: normalize apostrophes, geresh/gershayim, dashes and whitespace
detect likely source language when Latin spelling is not English
apply longest grapheme or marked-letter rules before single-letter rules
generate several weighted candidates instead of one irreversible output
compare normalized original, transliteration candidates and phonetic skeletons
send uncertain high-similarity cases to REVIEW

ranking_guidance.rule: Multiply or sum log-weights across a candidate; retain top-N distinct normalized forms.

decision_safety.BLOCK: Use only for exact normalized matches or a very high-confidence verified alias/phonetic duplicate.
decision_safety.REVIEW: Use when a plausible transliteration candidate matches but pronunciation, origin or word boundary is ambiguous.
decision_safety.ALLOW: Use only after exact, normalized, transliterated and phonetic candidate searches all remain below threshold.
